$comment: Phase 03 §A–Z acceptance criteria, the 20 architectural invariants, the W acceptance list and the X Definition of Done resolved against repository artefacts. Verified four ways: pasted document, architecture/phase-03-multi-tenancy.md, frontend/src/lib/kernel/phase-contracts/phase-03-multi-tenancy.ts, architecture/registry.json.

documentIntegrity.finding: The pasted Phase 03 document is complete and internally consistent (A–Z, 20 invariants, DoD, acceptance). No empty sections were found.

ownership.note: Phase 03 owns tenancy boundaries: registry, lifecycle, context, isolation, routing, topology, configuration, quotas, entitlements, ownership metadata, migration/provisioning coordination, residency. It never owns identity (02), security enforcement (08/09), domain reality (04), financial truth (13) or data infrastructure (14).

areas.requirement: A canonical tenant registry with the eight lifecycle states, tenant types, immutable ids and hierarchy.

areas.area: Tenant lifecycle engine (C2) — provisioning through termination
areas.requirement: Creation, provisioning, activation, suspension, migration, archival and termination are validated, authorized, recorded and observable transitions.
Every request resolves to a tenant_id or is explicitly platform_scope/public_scope/cross_tenant_scope.
No tenant may reach another tenant's resources merely because both exist on the platform.
Tenant-owned tables enforce tenant-aware RLS so application defects cannot cross tenants.

areas.area: Tenant quotas (C8/P1–P5) — soft, hard, burst and fairness
areas.requirement: Storage, compute, API, AI inference, agent execution and messaging limits with soft warnings, hard blocks, burst capacity and inter-tenant fairness.
Tenant + Capability + Policy + Contract = Entitlement Decision, with expiry and auditable revocation.
Feature activation is tenant-scoped and cannot bypass mandatory platform security controls.
Provisioning is approval-gated and idempotent: repeated requests must not create duplicate environments.
Cross-tenant access must be explicit, authorized, scoped, auditable and policy-controlled; it is never ordinary tenant data.
TenantCreated, TenantProvisioned, TenantActivated, TenantSuspended, TenantMigrated, TenantArchived and TenantTerminated are typed and versioned.
Parent/child/peer/regional/federated relationships are modelled, and hierarchy never implies unrestricted descendant access.
Tenant placement supports jurisdiction, latency, compliance and capacity constraints without making geography synonymous with tenant identity.
One tenant must not consume unlimited shared resources at the expense of others; tenant isolation must survive load.

Determinable tenant boundary per resource; context never trusted from a client; identity and tenancy separate; no re-created authentication; isolation across sync and async; boundaries survive APIs, events, queues, caches, workflows and agents; cross-tenant explicit and auditable; canonical stable ids with mutable names; deletion covers derived copies; migration reversible until commit; configuration cannot bypass platform controls; hierarchy grants nothing implicitly; agents inherit boundaries; boundaries testable; noisy neighbours contained; tenant configuration cannot modify global security; shared and dedicated infrastructure; global sovereignty compatibility.

areas.area: Queue, cache and event tenant boundaries (Invariants 05/06, J6–J8)
areas.requirement: Tenant boundaries must survive queues, caches and events — including agent execution and workflow retries.
areas.boundaryNote: Hand-verified 2026-09-14: the event outbox carries no tenantId and no queue or cache module exists, so no asynchronous path preserves a tenant boundary. Registered as owned debt (03).

areas.requirement: Termination is multi-step, revokes credentials and integrations, and covers derived copies (backups, caches, queues, indexes, object storage, logs, analytics) with verifiable evidence.
areas.boundaryNote: The lifecycle module models termination as a state; no deprovisioning engine, credential-revocation path or deletion evidence exists. Registered as owned debt (03).

areas.requirement: Every operational signal is attributable to tenant_id, region, service, environment and request_id, with per-tenant dashboards and self-service views.
areas.boundaryNote: The observability primitive carries tenantId and is tested, but no runtime path emits it, so tenant-attributable signals do not exist in production yet (same unwired finding as phase 01).

areas.area: Workspace projection (tenant visible in a surface)
areas.requirement: The tenancy capability is projected in at least one workspace from real state (L4).
areas.boundaryNote: Closed 2026-09-14 (P03-4), and moved out of the Scholar portal after the neutrality correction: `/super-admin/tenants` is the platform control plane, lists every tenant from real `cg_tenant` state through `listTenants` behind the super-admin gate, and registers tenants through the idempotent `registerTenant`. It declares no role list of its own.
